issues.legal_issue: The special method for assessing agricultural income tax on a person holding land for others applies only when that person holds the land on their behalf and those others have joint interests in the land or its agricultural income.
material_facts: The trustees were the legal owners of the trust estate and managed it under a will that gave them powers of absolute owners.
The will directed the trustees to pay specified annuities from the estate’s net rents and profits to individual beneficiaries.
Each annuitant had an individual interest in the agricultural income to the extent of that person’s annuity; the annuitants did not share an undivided interest in the land or income.
The assessing authority assessed the trustees on the total agricultural income received from the estate.
issues.conclusion: The trustees did not hold the land on behalf of the annuitants, and the annuitants were not jointly interested in the land or its agricultural income. The special assessment method therefore did not apply, and the trustees were liable to tax on the total agricultural income received by them; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 11(1) of the U.P. Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1948, the special assessment method applies when a person holds land as a common manager, receiver, administrator or the like on behalf of persons jointly interested in the land or its agricultural income. “On behalf of” denotes an agency or representative relationship, not merely holding property for another’s benefit. Under section 3 of the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, the trustee is the owner of trust property and the beneficiary has a right against the trustee as owner; accordingly, a trustee holds the property in the trustee’s own right, though for the beneficiaries’ benefit. “Jointly interested” denotes an undivided interest, rather than separate individual interests. Sections 2(11) and 3 of the U.P. Act establish the general definition of a person and the charging liability. Lister v. Pickford was considered but distinguished because its observations concerned limitation and adverse possession.

rule.if: agricultural_income_tax_assessment and trustee_is_legal_owner and trustee_holds_for_benefit_not_as_agent and beneficiaries_have_separate_interests

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_assessment: An agricultural income tax assessment concerns income derived from land managed or held by a trustee for beneficiaries.
predicates.trustee_is_legal_owner: The trustee holds legal ownership of the trust property.
predicates.trustee_holds_for_benefit_not_as_agent: The trustee holds the property for the beneficiaries’ benefit but does not hold it as their agent or representative.
predicates.beneficiaries_have_separate_interests: Each beneficiary has an individual interest in the property’s income rather than an undivided interest shared with the other beneficiaries.

issues.definition: When an agricultural income tax assessment concerns a trustee who is the legal owner, holds for beneficiaries’ benefit rather than as their agent, and serves beneficiaries with separate interests, the trustee is assessed on the total agricultural income.
